I am a 60-year-old woman farming here in Oromia, and this small maize plot of mine is close to the homestead. It is only a small piece, but maize feeds my family, so I must take care of it well. I will go to the cooperative for some DAP and urea if the supply comes in time — my son helps me carry it. I keep a few cattle, so I spread manure from the kraal before the rains, and I buy improved maize seed from the cooperative when I can afford it because it gives better cobs than the seed I save. I do not have irrigation here, we wait for the meher rains like everyone. Most of the work I do myself with my daughter-in-law, but for planting and weeding I call on two young men from the village for a few days because my back is not what it used to be.
